item.title: Leoru hat-trick fires Navua to 3-0 win over Nadi in FMF IDC opener
item.description: Walter Leoru was the hero for Vantex Solutions Navua FC after scoring a hat-trick in their 3-0 victory over Pacific Heavy Industries Nadi FC in their opening FMF Inter-District Championship match at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva. Leoru delivered an impressive performance to secure all three goals for Navua and give his side a strong start to their campaign .
item.content:encoded:
Walter Leoru was the hero for Vantex Solutions Navua FC after scoring a hat-trick in their 3-0 victory over Pacific Heavy Industries Nadi FC in their opening FMF Inter-District Championship match at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

Leoru delivered an impressive performance to secure all three goals for Navua and give his side a strong start to their campaign .

Navua Head Coach Rodeck Singh praised Leoru's performance, saying the striker showed why the team continues to have confidence in him.

Singh says the victory was particularly pleasing as Navua had been affected by several injuries and player absences heading into the match .

He says the return of several players, including Bula FC players and key defenders, has strengthened the side.

Navua will now turn their attention to their next match against Ba, which Singh expects to be a fiery encounter.

He has called on Navua supporters to come out in numbers and back the team.

Nadi was reduced to 10 men after Shaheel Valentine received a red card.

item.title: Bale’s hard work earns him a step closer to his Drua dream
item.description: For Queen Victoria School youngster Viliame Tuilaucala Bale, years of hard work and dedication are paying off as he takes another big step in his rugby journey by joining the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua Development squad. Bale has been part of the Fijian Drua's development pathway since he was first identified while attending Labasa College.
item.content:encoded:
For Queen Victoria School youngster Viliame Tuilaucala Bale, years of hard work and dedication are paying off as he takes another big step in his rugby journey by joining the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua Development squad.

Bale has been part of the Fijian Drua's development pathway since he was first identified while attending Labasa College.

He was selected among 29 players for the club's inaugural Under-16 Academy intake and later became part of the inaugural Drua Academy programme in 2024.

The proud son of Kocoma in Cakaudrove, with maternal links to Dawa in Cakaudrove , Bale continued to impress through the schoolboy ranks.

He recently represented the Queen Victoria School Under-18 side in the 2026 Vodafone Deans Competition before earning the opportunity to move into the Drua Development squad.

Bale says he is grateful to God for blessing him with his talent and for opening the opportunity for him.

He also thanked his parents for their support throughout his journey and his school friends for constantly pushing him to be at his best.

Bale says he is excited about the opportunity and is looking forward to training and playing with the senior development team.

Fijian Drua Director of Development and Pathways Nemani Nadolo-Kuridrani says Bale is a talented young player who has been in the Drua pathway for some time.

Nadolo-Kuridrani says Bale was identified at a young age and has continued to work hard and develop his game.

He says Bale's progression is exactly what the Drua pathway is designed to achieve by identifying talented young players from around Fiji, investing in their development and giving them opportunities to progress within the Drua system.

Bale's journey from schoolboy rugby and the Drua Academy into the Development squad highlights the pathway available for young players to work towards the professional game.

item.title: Shankar cleared for FMF IDC, decision on Mani still pending
item.description: Rewa defender Delon Shankar has been cleared to play in the FMF Inter-District Championship after the Fiji Football Association Board decided to place him on a one-year good behaviour bond. Fiji Football Association says the decision was made following consultations with coaches, and Rewa has been informed.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa defender Delon Shankar has been cleared to play in the FMF Inter-District Championship after the Fiji Football Association Board decided to place him on a one-year good behaviour bond.

Fiji Football Association says the decision was made following consultations with coaches, and Rewa has been informed.

However, Shankar has suffered setbacks in his pursuit of professional football opportunities.

His nomination for a placement with the Oceania Football Confederation in Auckland has been withdrawn, while his offer from Bula FC has also been withdrawn.

Fiji FA says the Bula FC coach will decide at a later stage whether Shankar will be given a second opportunity to join the club.

Fiji FA says Shankar needs to improve his behaviour and professionalism if he wants to pursue a professional football career.

It says issues such as failing to inform the relevant parties and leaving without permission need to be addressed.

Meanwhile, a decision on suspended Labasa player Melvin Mani is yet to be made.

Labasa has been asked to provide its views and any relevant documents before the Fiji FA Board decides whether Mani will be allowed to feature in the FMF IDC.

Fiji FA also thanked FMF for sponsoring the tournament and encouraged fans to attend the matches over the long weekend.
